messages.content: What does "punctual" mean? Also, why do teachers ask us to revise before a test?

1. Punctual means arriving at the right time, not late.
2. Revising helps you remember what you learned, so it is easier to recall in the test.
Fix this sentence: She don't like spicy food. And why does milk turn sour if left out?

1. She doesn't like spicy food. Why: subject-verb agreement ("she" -> "doesn't").
2. Warm air helps germs in the milk grow, and they make it sour.
meaning of "tidy"? and what is a good way to remember where I put my keys

1. Tidy means neat and in good order.
2. Always put them in the same place, like a hook near the door.
Could you tell me what "drizzle" means, and why the road smells nice after the first rain?

1. Drizzle is very light, fine rain.
2. Rain on dry soil lets out a fresh smell that we notice in the air.
1) Correct this: He go to school with his friends yesterday. 2) My friend is sad today, what can I say to her?

1. He went to school with his friends yesterday. Why: past tense ("yesterday" -> "went").
2. You can say, "I am here if you want to talk," and then listen without hurrying her.
What is a "passenger"? Also why do we keep our bags close in a crowded train station?

1. A passenger is a person who travels in a vehicle but does not drive it.
2. In a crowd it is easy to lose a bag or have it taken, so keeping it close keeps it safe.
Is it "fewer" or "less" in: There are less players today? Also, why do players stretch before a game?

1. There are fewer players today. Why: word choice ("less" -> "fewer" for things you can count).
2. Stretching warms up the muscles, which helps them move well and lowers the chance of a sprain.
Tell me what "generous" means. Also, how can I help my mother in the kitchen without being asked?

1. Generous means happy to give or share with others.
2. You could wash the vegetables or lay the plates, because small jobs save her time.
What does "hygiene" mean and why do we wash hands before eating?

1. Hygiene means keeping yourself and your things clean so you stay well.
2. Soap and water remove germs from your hands, so they do not go into your mouth with the food.
What is "decorate"? Also, my little cousin cries at loud crackers during Diwali, what could I do?

1. To decorate is to make a place look nicer by adding pretty things.
2. Take her to a quieter room, hold her hand, and let her cover her ears or watch from a distance.
Correct this sentence please: I have two book on my table. And what does "chapter" mean?

1. I have two books on my table. Why: plural ("two" -> "books").
2. A chapter is one main part of a book, usually with its own number or title.
Why do leaves fall in autumn? And what is the meaning of "fragile"?

1. The tree stops feeding its leaves when days get shorter and cooler, so they dry up and drop.
2. Fragile means easy to break or damage, like a thin glass.
What does "thrifty" mean? Also, I want a new bag but I already have one, what should I think about?

1. Thrifty means careful about spending and not wasting things.
2. Ask yourself if your old bag still works. If it does, you can wait and see whether you still want the new one later.
Fix this: Me and my boss was in the meeting. Also, what should I do if I do not understand a task?

1. My boss and I were in the meeting. Why: pronoun ("Me" -> "I"); subject-verb agreement ("was" -> "were").
2. Ask the person who gave it to you to explain it again. It is better to ask early than to do it wrongly.
What is "nervous"? and how do I stay calm before speaking in class

1. Nervous means worried or a little afraid about something that is going to happen.
2. Breathe slowly a few times and practise your first sentence, because a good start makes the rest easier.
What does "nocturnal" mean? Also, why do dogs wag their tails?

1. Nocturnal means active at night, like owls and bats.
2. A wagging tail is one way a dog shows its mood, and often it means the dog is excited or happy.
Why do we need to sleep before exams? Also, spell "necessary" for me.

1. Sleep helps your brain store what you studied and keeps you alert during the paper.
2. It is spelled n-e-c-e-s-s-a-r-y, with one c and two s.
I wrote: Rahul have eaten his lunch already. Is that right? And what does "ripe" mean?

1. No. It should be: Rahul has eaten his lunch already. Why: subject-verb agreement ("Rahul" -> "has").
2. Ripe means fully grown and ready to eat, like a soft, sweet mango.
What does "luggage" mean, and what should I do if I miss my bus?

1. Luggage is the bags and cases you carry when you travel.
2. Ask the bus staff or station desk when the next bus leaves, and tell someone at home where you are.
Is "furnitures" correct? Also, why does a room feel cooler when the fan is on?

1. No, it should be "furniture". Why: uncountable noun ("furnitures" -> "furniture").
2. The fan moves the air over your skin, which helps your sweat dry and makes you feel cooler.
Can you explain "loyal"? One more thing: my friend keeps borrowing my pens and never returns them. What should I do?

1. Loyal means staying faithful and supportive to a friend or a cause.
2. Tell him kindly that you need your pens back, and ask him to return them by the end of the day.
Why is it hot at noon and cooler in the evening? Also what does "humid" mean?

1. At noon the sun is high and its rays are strong, and by evening the sun is lower and the ground has cooled.
2. Humid means the air feels damp because it holds a lot of water.
Please fix: Priya run faster than me. And what does "stamina" mean?

1. Priya runs faster than me. Why: subject-verb agreement ("Priya" -> "runs").
2. Stamina is the strength to keep doing something for a long time without getting tired.
How do I say sorry to my sister after a fight? And what is the meaning of "sibling"?

1. Tell her plainly what you did wrong and that you are sorry, then give her time to answer.
2. A sibling is your brother or sister.
What does "posture" mean? And why should we drink water in summer?

1. Posture is the way you hold your body when you sit or stand.
2. You lose water through sweat in the heat, and drinking water replaces it so you stay fresh.
Fix this sentence: We goes to the temple on Navratri. Also, why do people light lamps at festivals?

1. We go to the temple on Navratri. Why: subject-verb agreement ("We" -> "go").
2. Lamps spread light and make the place look bright and joyful, and many people feel they bring good cheer.
meaning of "sequel" please. also how can i read more if i get bored easily?

1. A sequel is a book or film that continues the story of an earlier one.
2. Start with short books on things you like, and read for ten minutes a day instead of forcing long sessions.
What does "habitat" mean? Also, why do birds fly south in winter?

1. A habitat is the natural place where an animal or plant lives.
2. Many birds move to warmer places in winter because food becomes scarce in the cold.
What is a "budget"? And do I need to tell my parents if I lose my pocket money?

1. A budget is a plan for how much you will spend and how much you will save.
2. Yes, tell them honestly, because they can help you work out what to do next time.
Correct this: He is more taller than his brother. Also, what is a "colleague"?

1. He is taller than his brother. Why: comparative ("more taller" -> "taller").
2. A colleague is a person you work with.
What does "lonely" mean? and what can I do when i feel left out at lunch

1. Lonely means feeling sad because you are alone or have no one to share time with.
2. Ask one classmate if you can sit with them, or invite someone who is sitting alone.
Why do cats purr? And fix: The birds is singing in the tree.

1. Cats often purr when they feel content, and sometimes also to calm themselves.
2. The birds are singing in the tree. Why: subject-verb agreement ("birds" -> "are").
What is the difference between "principal" and "principle"? Also should I copy my friend's homework if I am out of time?

1. A principal is the head of a school; a principle is a basic rule or belief.
2. No, it is better to hand in what you finished and tell your teacher honestly. Copying does not help you learn.
Why do we chew food slowly? Also what does "nutritious" mean?

1. Chewing breaks food into small pieces so it is easier to swallow and digest.
2. Nutritious food has the things your body needs to grow and stay strong.
Spell "neighbour" for me. And why should we switch off lights when we leave a room?

1. It is n-e-i-g-h-b-o-u-r.
2. It saves electricity, which is useful because power is not free and should not be wasted.
What does "itinerary" mean? Also how do I stay safe when I travel alone by bus?

1. An itinerary is a plan of the places you will visit and when.
2. Sit near the front, keep your bag with you, and tell a family member your route and arrival time.
Fix this: She said me that she was late. Also, what is a "rumour"?

1. She told me that she was late. Why: word choice ("said me" -> "told me").
2. A rumour is a story people pass around that may not be true.
Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder? Another thing, what does "overcast" mean?

1. Light travels much faster than sound, so you see the flash first and hear the sound later.
2. Overcast means the sky is fully covered with grey cloud.
Why do we sweat when we play? And correct: I am playing cricket since morning.

1. Sweating cools your body down when it gets hot from moving.
2. I have been playing cricket since morning. Why: perfect tense ("since morning" -> "have been playing").
Meaning of "elderly"? And how can I make my grandmother feel included in our game night?

1. Elderly means old, and it is a polite word for older people.
2. Pick a game she knows or likes, sit next to her, and ask for her advice during the game.
What is a "habit"? Also why is it hard to wake up early after a late night?

1. A habit is something you do so often that you do it without thinking.
2. Your body is used to its sleep time, so it feels tired if you wake before it has rested enough.
Fix this: Diwali are my favourite festival. And what does "celebrate" mean?

1. Diwali is my favourite festival. Why: subject-verb agreement ("Diwali" -> "is").
2. To celebrate is to do something special and happy for an event or a day.
What does "narrator" mean? One more, is it okay to write in my own book?

1. A narrator is the person or voice who tells the story.
2. Yes, it is your book, so you can underline or make notes. Use a pencil if you may want to erase later.
Why do plants need sunlight? Also fix: There is many trees in the park.

1. Plants use sunlight to make their own food, and without it they cannot grow well.
2. There are many trees in the park. Why: subject-verb agreement ("many trees" -> "are").
What does "borrow" mean? And what should I do if I find a coin on the road?

1. To borrow is to take something for a short time and give it back later.
2. Keep it if nobody is around to ask, or give it to a shopkeeper if it looks like someone just dropped it.
Fix: Our manager give us the notes yesterday. Also tell me what "deadline" means.

1. Our manager gave us the notes yesterday. Why: past tense ("yesterday" -> "gave").
2. A deadline is the time by which a job must be finished.
Why do we cry when we are happy? Also what is the meaning of "grateful"?

1. Strong feelings, good or bad, can make the body let out tears.
2. Grateful means feeling thankful for something someone did or gave.
What does "herbivore" mean? Also should I feed biscuits to the street dog near my house?

1. A herbivore is an animal that eats only plants.
2. It is better not to, because dogs need proper food. A little water or plain rice is kinder.
Fix this sentence: I am agree with you. And why is it good to ask questions in class?

1. I agree with you. Why: extra word ("am" -> remove).
2. Questions clear up what you did not understand, and other students often have the same doubt.
Please help me with two things. What does "curious" mean? And what is a smart way to plan a study timetable?

1. Curious means wanting to know or learn about things.
2. List your subjects, give harder ones more time, and add short breaks so you do not get tired.
Is "alot" a word? Also my friend is angry with me and will not talk. What now?

1. No, it is two words: "a lot". Why: spelling ("alot" -> "a lot").
2. Give her some time, then say you are sorry for what upset her and ask if you can talk.
Tell me what "bland" means, and why does bread get hard if left open?

1. Bland means having little or no taste.
2. The air dries out the moisture in the bread, so it turns hard and stale.
Fix: We reached to the station early. Also, what is a "platform" at a station?

1. We reached the station early. Why: extra word ("to" -> remove).
2. A platform is the raised area beside the track where passengers wait for a train.
Why does a pressure cooker whistle? And what does "cozy" mean?

1. Steam builds up inside and escapes through the small vent, which makes the whistle sound.
2. Cozy means warm, comfortable and pleasant.
Why do we carry an umbrella in the monsoon? Also, how do you spell "separate"?

1. An umbrella keeps you dry, because the rain can make your clothes and books wet.
2. It is s-e-p-a-r-a-t-e, with an "a" in the middle, not an "e".
Correct this: Their team have won the match. And what does "opponent" mean?

1. Their team has won the match. Why: subject-verb agreement ("team" -> "has").
2. An opponent is the person or team you play against.
What does "inherit" mean? And my younger brother keeps copying me. Should I be annoyed?

1. To inherit is to receive something, like money or a trait, from a parent or relative.
2. It is normal to feel annoyed, but copying is often how little ones show they look up to you. You can calmly ask him to find his own style.
Can you tell me what "stretch" means? Also why does our heart beat faster when we run?

1. To stretch is to make your body or a muscle longer by pulling it out.
2. Your muscles need more oxygen when you run, so the heart pumps blood faster to bring it.
I wrote: On Holi we plays with colours. Please fix. And what is the meaning of "tradition"?

1. On Holi we play with colours. Why: subject-verb agreement ("we" -> "play").
2. A tradition is a custom that families or groups have followed for a long time.
What does "plot" mean in a story? And how do I choose a book from a big library?

1. The plot is the series of events that make up a story.
2. Read the back cover and the first page, and pick the one that makes you want to keep reading.
Meaning of "erosion"? Also, why is the sky blue?

1. Erosion is the slow wearing away of soil or rock by water, wind or ice.
2. Air spreads the blue part of sunlight more than the other colours, so the sky looks blue.
What does "expensive" mean? And is it fine to save a little from my pocket money each week?

1. Expensive means costing a lot of money.
2. Yes, saving a small amount each week is a good habit and it adds up for something you really want.
How do I politely say no to extra work? And what does "resign" mean?

1. You can say, "I would like to help, but I already have too much work this week."
2. To resign is to officially leave your job.
Fix this: I feeled very happy yesterday. Also, what is "jealous"?

1. I felt very happy yesterday. Why: verb form ("feeled" -> "felt").
2. Jealous means unhappy because someone has something you want.
What does "migrate" mean? And why do cows chew even when they are not eating?

1. To migrate is to move from one place to another, as birds do each season.
2. Cows bring up food from the first part of the stomach and chew it again to digest it well.
Why is it better to start homework early? And what does "assignment" mean?

1. Starting early gives you time to fix mistakes and ask for help, so you are not rushed.
2. An assignment is a piece of work given to you to do, like homework.
Fix: I want a apple and an banana. Also why do onions make us cry?

1. I want an apple and a banana. Why: article ("a apple" -> "an apple"; "an banana" -> "a banana").
2. Cutting an onion lets out a gas that stings the eyes, and the eyes make tears to wash it away.
What is "customs" at an airport? And what should I pack in a small day bag for a trip to the zoo?

1. Customs is the place where officers check what people bring into a country.
2. Pack water, a snack, a hat and a small towel. Keep it light so it is easy to carry.
Can you explain what "chore" means? And how can we share house work fairly?

1. A chore is a small regular job around the house, like sweeping or washing dishes.
2. Make a list and let everyone choose some tasks, then swap them each week so no one gets stuck with the worst ones.
What does "trust" mean? Also how do I make a new friend in a new school?

1. Trust means believing that a person is honest and will not hurt you.
2. Smile, say hello, and ask something simple like what game they like. Small talk is a good start.
Why does fog form on cold mornings? Also correct this: It is raining since morning.

1. Cold air cannot hold as much water, so the water in it turns into tiny drops that float near the ground.
2. It has been raining since morning. Why: perfect tense ("since morning" -> "has been raining").
What does "referee" mean? And why should we shake hands after a match?

1. A referee is the person who makes sure the players follow the rules.
2. It shows respect for the other team, whether you won or lost.
Tell me the meaning of "relatives". Also, how can I help when my father comes home tired?

1. Relatives are people who belong to your family, like aunts, uncles and cousins.
2. Greet him warmly, bring him a glass of water, and let him rest before you ask for anything.
Please correct: She have a headache today. What does "rest" mean when a person is ill?

1. She has a headache today. Why: subject-verb agreement ("She" -> "has").
2. Rest means to stop work or play and relax so the body can feel better.
What does "rangoli" mean? Why do people wear new clothes at festivals?

1. A rangoli is a colourful pattern made on the floor with powder, rice or flowers.
2. New clothes make the day feel special, and they are a way to show joy.
Is it "your" or "you're" in: Your very kind? And what makes a story interesting?

1. It should be: You're very kind. Why: apostrophe ("Your" -> "You're" meaning "you are").
2. A character we care about, a problem to solve and some surprises make a story interesting.
What is a "canopy" in a forest? Also why do some trees lose their leaves and others do not?

1. The canopy is the top layer of branches and leaves that forms a roof over the forest.
2. Some trees drop leaves to save water in dry or cold seasons, while others have tough leaves that last all year.
What does "discount" mean? And should I tell the shopkeeper if he gives me too much change?

1. A discount is a lower price than usual.
2. Yes, tell him, because it is honest and the extra money is not yours.
Fix: I will call you when I will reach the office. What does "punctuality" mean at work?

1. I will call you when I reach the office. Why: present tense ("when I will reach" -> "when I reach").
2. Punctuality means arriving and finishing on time.
What does "embarrassed" mean? And how can I feel better after I forget my lines in a play?

1. Embarrassed means feeling shy or uncomfortable because of something that happened in front of others.
2. Remember that everyone forgets sometimes, and most people soon forget it. Practise once more and try again.
Why do bees buzz? And correct: My dog is more friendlier than my cat.

1. The sound comes from their wings beating very fast.
2. My dog is friendlier than my cat. Why: comparative ("more friendlier" -> "friendlier").
How do you spell "beautiful"? One more: how can I stop talking in class?

1. It is b-e-a-u-t-i-f-u-l.
2. Sit away from your chatty friends and save your talk for break time. A small reminder note on your desk helps.
What does "leftover" mean? Also should I eat fruit before or after dinner?

1. Leftover food is what remains after a meal is finished.
2. Either is fine. Eat it when you feel comfortable, as long as you still enjoy your meal.
Fix this: There is two chairs in the room. Also why does a wet floor feel slippery?

1. There are two chairs in the room. Why: subject-verb agreement ("two chairs" -> "are").
2. Water makes a thin layer between the shoe and the floor, so there is less grip.
What does "delay" mean? Another thing, my train is late and I am bored. What can I do?

1. A delay is a time when something happens later than planned.
2. Read a book, listen to music with low volume, or chat with a family member. Keep an eye on the announcements.
Fix: My friend and me went to the market. What does "honest" mean?

1. My friend and I went to the market. Why: pronoun ("me" -> "I").
2. Honest means telling the truth and not cheating.
Why does the ground feel hot at noon? And what is the meaning of "breeze"?

1. The sun heats the ground all morning, so by noon it has taken in a lot of heat.
2. A breeze is a gentle, light wind.
Why is warming up needed? Also, is "practise" or "practice" right in: I practice football daily?

1. Warming up gets your muscles ready, which helps you play better and avoid injury.
2. In British spelling, the verb is "practise", so write: I practise football daily. In American spelling, "practice" is used for both.
Meaning of "cousin"? Why do older people tell stories?

1. A cousin is the child of your aunt or uncle.
2. Stories pass on memories and lessons, and they are a way to spend time with the young.
Can I ask what "energetic" means? And why do we yawn?

1. Energetic means full of strength and ready to do things.
2. People often yawn when they feel tired or bored, but scientists are still not sure of the full reason.
Fix this: Everyone were happy at the wedding. Also, what does "guest" mean?

1. Everyone was happy at the wedding. Why: subject-verb agreement ("Everyone" -> "was").
2. A guest is a person who is invited to your home or event.
What is a "biography"? And is it rude to fold the corner of a page?

1. A biography is a book about the life of a real person.
2. It can damage the page, so it is kinder to use a bookmark, especially for a library book.
Meaning of "puddle"? Also why do frogs croak after rain?

1. A puddle is a small pool of water on the ground.
2. Rain makes the ground wet and many frogs call out to find a mate at that time.
What does "earn" mean? And how can I save money for a gift for my teacher?

1. To earn is to get money for work that you do.
2. Set aside a small amount each week and keep it in a jar. Decide on a gift that fits what you have saved.
Correct this: He work in a bank since five years. Also, what is a "salary"?

1. He has worked in a bank for five years. Why: perfect tense ("work" -> "has worked"); preposition ("since" -> "for").
2. A salary is the fixed pay a person gets for work, usually each month.
What does "calm" mean? How do I handle a bad mood before school?

1. Calm means quiet and relaxed, not upset.
2. Take a few slow breaths, drink some water, and tell someone how you feel. A short walk can help too.
Why do hens cluck? Also fix: The elephant are very big.

1. Hens cluck to talk to each other and to their chicks.
2. The elephant is very big. Why: subject-verb agreement ("elephant" -> "is").
Tell me what "summarize" means. Also, why do we line up before entering class?

1. To summarize is to tell the main points of something in a short way.
2. Lining up keeps things orderly, so no one pushes and everyone enters safely.
What does "recipe" mean? And why should I wash fruit before eating it?

1. A recipe is a list of ingredients and steps for making a dish.
2. Washing removes dust and dirt from the skin, so they do not get into your mouth.
What does "melody" mean? And how do I practise a song when I keep making mistakes?

1. A melody is the tune of a song, the notes that you hum.
2. Play it slowly in small parts and repeat the hard part until it feels easy, then join the parts.
Why must plants get water every day in summer? Also, what is "compost"?

1. The heat dries the soil fast, and plants lose water through their leaves.
2. Compost is rotted kitchen and garden waste that is added to soil to feed plants.
Fix: How much costs this pen? And what does "bargain" mean?

1. How much does this pen cost? Why: question form ("costs" -> "does ... cost").
2. A bargain is something you buy for less than its usual price.
I am hosting a small party. What does "RSVP" mean on an invitation? And what snacks suit children?

1. RSVP means please reply to say whether you will come.
2. Fruit pieces, plain sandwiches and popcorn are easy, and check if any guest has a food allergy.
Why does grass have dew in the morning? Also what is the meaning of "dawn"?

1. At night the air cools and the water in it turns into small drops on the grass.
2. Dawn is the time when the sky starts to get light before sunrise.
Fix this sentence: The stars shines brightly last night. And why do we see the moon at night?

1. The stars shone brightly last night. Why: past tense ("last night" -> "shone").
2. The moon reflects light from the sun, and at night the dark sky makes that light easy to see.
What is a "signal" on the road? Also why should we wait for the green light even when no car is coming?

1. A signal is a light or sign that tells drivers and walkers when to stop or go.
2. A car could come suddenly, and following the rule keeps everyone in the habit of staying safe.
What does "hobby" mean? And how can I find a hobby I enjoy?

1. A hobby is something you do for fun in your free time.
2. Try a few things, like drawing, cycling or cooking, and keep the one you look forward to.
Spell "February" for me please. And why do we have a break in the middle of the school day?

1. It is F-e-b-r-u-a-r-y, with an "r" before the "u".
2. Breaks let your mind rest and your body move, so you can learn better afterwards.
Is it "between you and I" or "between you and me"? Also, what is a good gift for a friend who likes drawing?

1. It is "between you and me". Why: pronoun ("I" -> "me" after "between").
2. A good set of coloured pencils or a sketchbook would be a thoughtful choice.
What is "souvenir"? Also how do I keep my phone charged on a long journey?

1. A souvenir is a small item you keep to remember a place or trip.
2. Carry a power bank and lower the screen brightness, and close apps you are not using.
What does "exercise" mean? Also why do I feel sleepy after a heavy lunch?

1. Exercise is any activity, like running or stretching, that keeps your body fit.
2. Your body works hard to digest a big meal, and that can make you feel slow and sleepy.
Why is it important to drink water during a match? One more: Fix: He don't want to play.

1. Sweating makes you lose water, so you need to drink to keep your energy up.
2. He doesn't want to play. Why: subject-verb agreement ("He" -> "doesn't").
What does "forecast" mean? Also should I carry a jacket if the sky looks dark?

1. A forecast is a prediction of what the weather will be like.
2. Yes, dark clouds often bring rain or a cold wind, and a jacket is easy to carry.
Fix this: He eat rice every day. Another thing, why does ice cream melt faster in the sun?

1. He eats rice every day. Why: subject-verb agreement ("He" -> "eats").
2. The sun's heat warms the ice cream and turns the solid into liquid.
What does "proud" mean? And how can I thank my parents for something big?

1. Proud means feeling very pleased about something good you or someone else has done.
2. Tell them in a card or in person what you are thankful for, using their names and a real example.
Please explain "fiction". Also should I finish a book I do not like?

1. Fiction is a story that is made up and not real.
2. You do not have to. If it is dull after a few chapters, you can put it down and try another book.
Why do rivers flow to the sea? And what is the meaning of "current" in the sea?

1. Water runs downhill because of gravity, and the sea is the lowest place it can reach.
2. A current is water that moves steadily in one direction.
What is "interest" when you keep money in a bank account? Also, how can I stop buying snacks too much?

1. Interest is extra money the bank pays you for keeping your money with it.
2. Carry a bottle of water and a homemade snack, and decide before you leave home how much to spend.
Is "I am working here from 2020" correct? And how can I ask my team for help?

1. No. Say: I have been working here since 2020. Why: perfect tense ("am working" -> "have been working"); preposition ("from" -> "since").
2. Say what you are stuck on and what you have already tried, then ask for a few minutes of their time.
Tell me what "disappointed" means. Also, how do I cheer up a friend who did badly in a test?

1. Disappointed means sad because something did not turn out as you hoped.
2. Tell him you are there for him, and offer to study together for the next one.
What does "predator" mean? Also why do cats like to sit in boxes?

1. A predator is an animal that hunts other animals for food.
2. Many cats feel safe and warm in small, closed spaces, and a box also hides them from view.
Correct this: My teacher give me many homework. Also what does "neat" handwriting mean?

1. My teacher gives me a lot of homework. Why: subject-verb agreement ("teacher" -> "gives"); uncountable noun ("many homework" -> "a lot of homework").
2. Neat handwriting is clear, tidy writing that is easy to read.
What does "leak" mean? And what should I do when the tap at home keeps dripping?

1. A leak is a small hole or gap through which water or air escapes.
2. Tell an adult at home so they can tighten it or call a plumber. Meanwhile, put a bowl under it.
Why do we exchange sweets at festivals? And what is "auspicious"?

1. Sharing sweets is a way to show love and wish people happiness.
2. Auspicious means a sign of good luck and a good start.
What is a "ticket"? Also, why should we keep our tickets until the journey ends?

1. A ticket is a small paper or card that shows you paid to travel or enter.
2. Staff may check it during or at the end of the trip, and you may need it as proof.
What does "argue" mean? And correct: I and my sister are twins.

1. To argue is to talk angrily with someone because you disagree.
2. My sister and I are twins. Why: word order ("I and my sister" -> "My sister and I").
Why do we clap to the beat? Also what is "rhythm"?

1. Clapping helps people keep time together and feel part of the music.
2. Rhythm is the pattern of beats in music or in a poem.
Fix: Their garden have many flowers. And why do bees visit flowers?

1. Their garden has many flowers. Why: subject-verb agreement ("garden" -> "has").
2. Bees collect sweet nectar from flowers to make honey.
What does "receipt" mean? And why should I check my bag before leaving the shop?

1. A receipt is a paper that shows what you bought and how much you paid.
2. You can make sure you have all your things and the right items before leaving, so there is no mix-up.
What is the meaning of "routine"? Also how can I wake up without feeling grumpy?

1. A routine is a set of things you do regularly in the same order.
2. Sleep at a fixed time, open the curtains for light, and drink water soon after you wake up.
Why are some people afraid of the dark? Also fix: I can't sleep, I am having a nightmare yesterday.

1. In the dark we cannot see what is around us, so the mind can imagine scary things.
2. I couldn't sleep because I had a nightmare yesterday. Why: past tense ("yesterday" -> "couldn't", "had"); conjunction (comma -> "because").
Meaning of "crowded"? Another thing: how do I find my way if I get lost in a market?

1. Crowded means full of people, with little free space.
2. Stay where you are and ask a shopkeeper or a police officer for help, then call your family.
What does "collect" mean? Fix this too: She collect stamps.

1. To collect is to gather things of one kind and keep them together.
2. She collects stamps. Why: subject-verb agreement ("She" -> "collects").
What does "absent" mean? Also should I tell my teacher if I did not understand a lesson?

1. Absent means not present, for example, missing from school.
2. Yes, because the teacher can explain it again, and the doubt will not grow.
What does "cooperate" mean? And why is it hard to say sorry?

1. To cooperate is to work together to reach a goal.
2. Saying sorry means admitting a mistake, and many people feel proud or scared about that.
Is "I am going for market" right? Also what should I carry on a hot day outing?

1. No. Say: I am going to the market. Why: preposition ("for" -> "to the").
2. Carry water, a cap or umbrella, and wear light cotton clothes.
What does "humidity" mean? And why do we feel sticky in the rains?

1. Humidity is the amount of water vapour in the air.
2. Damp air makes sweat dry slowly, so it stays on the skin.
What is a "champion"? Also, how do I handle losing a game?

1. A champion is a person or team that has won a competition.
2. Congratulate the winner, think about what to improve, and remember it is only a game.
Fix: My mother cook very tasty food. And what does "spice" mean?

1. My mother cooks very tasty food. Why: subject-verb agreement ("mother" -> "cooks").
2. A spice is a dried seed, root or bark, like cumin or pepper, that adds flavour to food.
What is "vitamin"? Also, why should I eat vegetables?

1. A vitamin is a small substance in food that your body needs to stay healthy.
2. Vegetables give your body fibre and many of the things it needs to grow.
Could you say what "procession" means? And how do I stay safe in a big festival crowd?

1. A procession is a line of people moving along in an organised way.
2. Stay with your family, agree on a meeting spot, and keep your belongings close.
What does "dictionary" mean? Another one: how do I choose a good time to read?

1. A dictionary is a book that tells you the meanings and spellings of words.
2. Pick a quiet time when you are not hungry or sleepy, such as just after homework.
Fix this: The river flow slowly. And what is a "waterfall"?

1. The river flows slowly. Why: subject-verb agreement ("river" -> "flows").
2. A waterfall is a place where a river drops from a height.
What does "save" mean when it is about money? And is it wrong to ask for a gift I really want?

1. To save is to keep money instead of spending it.
2. No, it is fine to ask politely. Just accept it kindly if the answer is no.
What does "teamwork" mean? Also how should I respond to a rude message from a coworker?

1. Teamwork is people working together towards the same goal.
2. Wait a little before you reply, then answer calmly and stick to the task. If it keeps happening, speak to your manager.
Fix: I am boring in this class. And what does "patient" mean here: be patient?

1. I am bored in this class. Why: verb form ("boring" -> "bored").
2. Here, patient means able to wait calmly without getting angry.
What is a "pet"? Also, how often should a dog be taken for a walk?

1. A pet is an animal that you keep at home for company.
2. It depends on the dog's age and breed, so ask a vet or the person who gave you the dog.
Why do we have a uniform? And is it "alright" or "all right"?

1. A uniform makes all students look the same, which helps them feel equal and makes it easy to know who belongs to the school.
2. Both forms are used, but "all right" is the safer choice in careful writing.
What was my teacher's name last year? And what does "diligent" mean?

1. I don't know your teacher's name, because I cannot see your school records. Your old notebooks or a classmate may remember.
2. Diligent means working carefully and with steady effort.
Will it rain at my house tomorrow? Also what does "gust" mean?

1. I can't check the weather, so I'm not sure. A weather report or an official forecast site will tell you.
2. A gust is a sudden strong rush of wind.
Correct this: Me and Arjun is best friends. Also, what makes a good friend?

1. Arjun and I are best friends. Why: pronoun ("Me" -> "I"); subject-verb agreement ("is" -> "are").
2. A good friend listens, tells the truth kindly and stays by you in hard times.
When is the next train to Pune? And what does "depart" mean?

1. I don't know, because I cannot see timetables. Check the railway's official site or ask at the station counter.
2. To depart is to leave, usually on a journey.
How can I tell if a mango is ripe? Also, correct: There is some apples in the basket.

1. Press it gently, since it should be a little soft, and a sweet smell near the stem is a good sign.
2. There are some apples in the basket. Why: subject-verb agreement ("apples" -> "are").
What does "spacious" mean? Also should I clean my room before guests arrive?

1. Spacious means having a lot of room inside.
2. Yes, a tidy room is pleasant for you and for the guests, and it takes only a few minutes to put things away.
Meaning of "dizzy"? And should I sit down if I feel like that?

1. Dizzy means feeling that the room is spinning or that you might fall.
2. Yes, sit down and tell an adult nearby. If it keeps happening, see a doctor.
Fix: We was winning the game. What is a "tournament"?

1. We were winning the game. Why: subject-verb agreement ("We" -> "were").
2. A tournament is a series of matches in which teams compete to find a winner.
What does "affection" mean? Another thing, my grandfather forgets things. How should I talk to him?

1. Affection is a gentle feeling of love and care for someone.
2. Speak slowly and kindly, repeat things without showing annoyance, and give him time to answer.
Define "pilgrimage" for me. Also, who made the sweets at my house yesterday?

1. A pilgrimage is a journey to a holy place.
2. I don't know, because I cannot see what happens in your home. Your family can tell you who cooked.
Fix this: She have lost her book. And what does "author" mean?

1. She has lost her book. Why: subject-verb agreement ("She" -> "has").
2. An author is the person who writes a book.
Why does a rainbow have colours? Also what does "mist" mean?

1. Raindrops split sunlight into its different colours, and we see them as bands in the sky.
2. Mist is a thin cloud of tiny water drops near the ground.
What is a "coupon"? Also, what is the best way to keep my pocket money safe?

1. A coupon is a small paper or code that gives you a lower price on something.
2. Keep it in a box or wallet at home, and carry only what you need for the day.
Fix: She go to office by bus every day. Also what does "promote" mean at work?

1. She goes to the office by bus every day. Why: subject-verb agreement ("She" -> "goes"); article (add "the" before "office").
2. To promote someone is to give them a higher job or rank.
What does "anxious" mean? And how can I calm down before a big match?

1. Anxious means worried and uneasy about something that may happen.
2. Take slow breaths, think about the fun of playing, and do your usual warm-up.
What does "mammal" mean? Also, why does my cat bring me dead mice?

1. A mammal is an animal that feeds its young with milk, like a cow or a human.
2. Cats are natural hunters, and some bring prey home to show it or share it.
What does "revise" mean? And when is my next exam?

1. To revise is to read over what you learned so you remember it.
2. I don't know, as I cannot see your school calendar. Check your timetable or ask your teacher.
Why does bread rise? Also, fix this: I am liking tea.

1. Yeast makes tiny gas bubbles in the dough, which push it up and make it soft.
2. I like tea. Why: verb form ("am liking" -> "like", since "like" is not used in continuous tense).
What does "direction" mean? Another question: how can I read a map in a new city?

1. A direction is the way you go, such as north or left.
2. Find where you are first, then look for a big road or landmark to follow and turn the map to face your way.
Is "I will do it by myself" correct? Also why does a house feel warm in the afternoon?

1. Yes, it is correct. Why: no error (pronoun: "by myself" is correct).
2. The walls and roof take in the sun's heat all day and the warmth builds up inside.
What does "apologise" mean? Why does my friend not text me back sometimes?

1. To apologise is to say that you are sorry.
2. I don't know the reason in your case. He may be busy or away from his phone, so you can ask him gently later.
Correct this: It is more hotter today. And what does "scorching" mean?

1. It is hotter today. Why: comparative ("more hotter" -> "hotter").
2. Scorching means extremely hot.
What does "fair play" mean? And why should I not be rude when my team loses?

1. Fair play means following the rules and treating others with respect in a game.
2. Being rude hurts people and spoils the day, and staying kind shows you can lose with grace.
Is it "grandparents" or "grand parents"? Also, how can I help look after a baby cousin?

1. It is one word: "grandparents". Why: spelling ("grand parents" -> "grandparents").
2. Stay near an adult, play gently, and never carry the baby alone unless an adult says it is fine.
What does "fever" mean? Also should I take medicine from a friend if I feel unwell?

1. A fever is a body temperature higher than usual, often when a person is ill.
2. No, please tell an adult or a doctor first, because medicine should only be taken when they say so.
Tell me what "lantern" means. Fix too: We lights the lamps yesterday.

1. A lantern is a light with a case around it that you can carry or hang.
2. We lit the lamps yesterday. Why: past tense ("yesterday" -> "lit").
What is a "poem"? And is it good to read aloud?

1. A poem is a short piece of writing that often uses rhythm and sometimes rhyme.
2. Yes, reading aloud helps you hear the words, improves your speaking and makes it easier to remember.
Fix: Many bird flies over the lake. And why do mountains have snow at the top?

1. Many birds fly over the lake. Why: plural ("bird" -> "birds"); subject-verb agreement ("flies" -> "fly").
2. The air gets colder as you go higher, so snow stays there even when the valley is warm.
What does "wealthy" mean? Another thing, what is the price of gold today?

1. Wealthy means having a lot of money or things of value.
2. I don't know, because I cannot see live prices. A jeweller or a trusted market website can tell you today's rate.
What does "schedule" mean? And how can I plan my day when I have too many tasks?

1. A schedule is a plan that shows what you will do and when.
2. Write all tasks, pick the most important ones first, and give each a time slot. Leave a gap for surprises.
Correct this sentence: I was very exciting about the trip. And what is "homesick"?

1. I was very excited about the trip. Why: verb form ("exciting" -> "excited").
2. Homesick means sad because you miss your home or family.
What does "endangered" mean? Also why do ants walk in a line?

1. Endangered means in danger of dying out completely.
2. Ants leave a scent trail, and the others follow it to find food.
Fix this: He is knowing the answer. Also, how do I keep my school bag tidy?

1. He knows the answer. Why: verb form ("is knowing" -> "knows").
2. Put books in order of your timetable, keep pens in a pouch, and empty the bag at the end of every week.
What does "flavour" mean? Another thing: is it okay to skip breakfast?

1. Flavour is the taste of food or drink.
2. It is better not to, because breakfast gives you energy for the morning. If you are not hungry, have something light like fruit.
Fix: Please close the window, it's very cold. Is the comma right? Also, what does "insulate" mean?

1. Not quite. It should be: Please close the window; it's very cold. Why: punctuation (comma -> semicolon between two sentences).
2. To insulate is to cover something so heat, cold or sound cannot easily pass through.
How far is Jaipur from my town? Also what does "journey" mean?

1. I don't know, as I do not know where your town is. A map or route planner will show the distance.
2. A journey is a trip from one place to another, usually a long one.
Meaning of "gossip"? Also should I join when others laugh at someone?

1. Gossip is talk about other people's private matters, often unkind or untrue.
2. No, because it hurts the person. You can stay quiet or change the topic.
First, what does "shade" mean? Then why is sunscreen useful?

1. Shade is a place where the sun's light is blocked, so it is cooler.
2. Sunscreen protects the skin from the sun's strong rays, which can burn it.
Fix this: Neither of the boys are ready. And what does "captain" mean in a team?

1. Neither of the boys is ready. Why: subject-verb agreement ("Neither" -> "is").
2. The captain is the leader of the team.
What does "orphan" mean? And how can I be kind to a classmate who lost a parent?

1. An orphan is a child who has lost both parents.
2. Be gentle, include them in games, and listen if they want to talk. You do not have to say the perfect thing.
What does "fit" mean when we say a person is fit? Also why should I brush my teeth at night?

1. Fit means healthy and strong enough to do physical things easily.
2. Brushing removes food left on your teeth so germs cannot damage them while you sleep.
What is "harvest"? Why do farmers celebrate Pongal?

1. A harvest is the time when ripe crops are gathered from the fields.
2. Pongal is a time to give thanks for the harvest, the sun and the cattle that help the farmers.
What does "sentence" mean in grammar? And how can I improve my handwriting?

1. A sentence is a group of words that makes a complete thought.
2. Write slowly, keep letters the same size, and practise a few lines each day.
Fix this: The sun rise in the east. Also, why is the sea salty?

1. The sun rises in the east. Why: subject-verb agreement ("sun" -> "rises").
2. Rivers carry small amounts of salt from rocks to the sea, and the water evaporates while the salt stays.
What does "afford" mean? And what should I do before I buy something online?

1. To afford something is to have enough money to pay for it.
2. Ask an adult first, read the full description, and check that the seller looks trustworthy.
Fix: He is working on the project since Monday. What does "deliver" mean in a work message?

1. He has been working on the project since Monday. Why: perfect tense ("is working since" -> "has been working since").
2. To deliver is to bring or hand over something, such as a finished task, on time.
Tell me what "confident" means. How can I become more confident in speaking English?

1. Confident means sure of yourself and your abilities.
2. Speak a little every day, even to yourself, and do not worry about small mistakes. Practice builds confidence.
Meaning of "flock"? Another thing, why do birds sit on wires?

1. A flock is a group of birds or sheep.
2. Wires give a good place to rest and look around, and the birds are not hurt because they touch only one wire.
What does "seed" mean? Also, how deep should I plant a bean seed?

1. A seed is the small part of a plant from which a new plant grows.
2. Plant it about two to three centimetres deep. The seed packet often gives the exact depth too.
Fix: There is a lot of cars on the road. And what does "pedestrian" mean?

1. There are a lot of cars on the road. Why: subject-verb agreement ("a lot of cars" -> "are").
2. A pedestrian is a person who travels on foot.
What does "customer" mean? And what should I do if the shopkeeper gives me the wrong item?

1. A customer is a person who buys things from a shop.
2. Show him the item and the receipt politely and ask him to change it.
Is "songs" spelled with an apostrophe in: Our songs' were nice? Also what does "chorus" mean?

1. No apostrophe is needed: Our songs were nice. Why: apostrophe ("songs'" -> "songs" for a plain plural).
2. A chorus is the part of a song that repeats, or a group of people who sing together.
How is "yacht" spelt? It looks odd. And what does "exhausted" mean?

1. It is y-a-c-h-t, and it is said like "yot". The "ch" is silent.
2. Exhausted means extremely tired. We were exhausted after the long hike.

What does "cautious" mean?
Do I put "a" or "an" before "hour"?

1. Cautious means careful to avoid danger or mistakes. Be cautious when you cross the road.
2. Say "an hour", because the "h" is silent and the word starts with a vowel sound. I waited for an hour.
What does it mean to "burn the midnight oil"? Also, what does "generous" mean?

1. It means to work or study late into the night. He burned the midnight oil before his test.
2. Generous means happy to give or share with others. Our neighbour is generous and always shares her mangoes.
What's a good way to dry wet shoes? And one more: What does "a fish out of water" mean?

1. Stuff them with old newspaper and leave them in a breezy, shady spot. Change the paper when it gets wet.
2. It means a person who feels uncomfortable in a new place. She felt like a fish out of water at the new school.

Two quick questions.
How do I spell "library"? People say "liberry".
What does "nephew" mean?

1. It is spelt l-i-b-r-a-r-y, with two "r"s. Say it slowly as li-brar-y so you hear both.
2. A nephew is the son of your brother or sister. My nephew visits us every summer.

How do I decide what to wear on a rainy day?
Also, how do I spell the word for the days when you are not at school, "vacation" or "vaccation"?

1. Choose clothes that dry quickly and shoes that do not slip. Carry an umbrella or a raincoat.
2. It is "vacation", with one "c" and one "t". We went to Goa for the vacation.
What does "too many cooks spoil the broth" mean? One more thing. How do I make a pot of dal?

1. It means that too many people working on one thing can ruin it. Let two of us plan, since too many cooks spoil the broth.
2. Wash the dal and boil it in water until it is soft. Add a pinch of turmeric and salt, then pour a tempering of cumin seeds over it.
Hi, I have two questions. How do I find a book in the library? What does "as busy as a bee" mean?

1. Ask the librarian or look up the title in the list. Then find the shelf by its number and look along the spines.
2. It means very busy. Mum is as busy as a bee before the festival.

What does "add fuel to the fire" mean?
And how do I find a word in a dictionary?

1. It means to make a bad situation worse. Shouting only added fuel to the fire.
2. Look at the first letter and go to that section. Then match the second letter and go on until you find the word.
How do I thread a needle? Also, I always get "fourty" wrong. Is it "forty"?

1. Wet the end of the thread and cut it straight. Hold the needle up to the light and pass the thread through the eye.
2. Yes, it is "forty", with no "u". But "four" and "fourteen" keep the "u".

what does "piece of cake" mean
How can I stop the pages of my book from getting wet in the rain?

1. It means something very easy to do. The quiz was a piece of cake.
2. Wrap the book in a plastic cover before you put it in your bag. Keep the bag close to your body under an umbrella.
What does "vehicle" mean? Also, what does "cry over spilt milk" mean?

1. A vehicle is something that carries people or goods on the road. A bus is a large vehicle.
2. It means to be upset about something that cannot be changed. It is done, so do not cry over spilt milk.

Two quick questions.
What does it mean to "cut corners"?
What does "meadow" mean?

1. It means to do a job in a quicker and poorer way. The builder cut corners, and the wall cracked.
2. A meadow is a field of grass and wild flowers. The cows grazed in the meadow.

Hello! Can you help me with these two?
How do I keep ants away from the sugar jar?
What does "close call" mean?

1. Keep the jar tightly closed and wipe up any crumbs. You can also stand it in a dish of water.
2. It means a narrow escape from danger or trouble. The bike skidded, but it was a close call and nobody was hurt.

is it ok to say "me and my sister" at the start of a sentence?
Also, how do I clean muddy shoes?

1. It is better to say "My sister and I" when you are the one doing the action. My sister and I went to the market.
2. Let the mud dry and brush it off. Then wipe the shoes with a damp cloth.
What's the best way to pack a lunch box? One more thing. what does "go with the flow" mean?

1. Pack the main food in a closed box, and put anything wet, like curry, in a small leak-proof tub. Add a fruit and a spoon.
2. It means to accept things as they come and not worry. We will go with the flow on the trip.
Quick doubts from my homework. How do I spell "Tuesday"? What's an easy way to keep a diary?

1. It is T-u-e-s-d-a-y. Write it with a capital "T" every time.
2. Write a few lines each night about what happened. Include the date and one thing that made you happy.

What does "scarce" mean?
And is it "grammer" or "grammar"?

1. Scarce means hard to find because there is not enough. Water is scarce in the dry season.
2. It is "grammar", ending in "-ar". Our grammar test is on Friday.
How do I spell "success"? What does "confident" mean?

1. It is s-u-c-c-e-s-s, with a double "c" and a double "s" at the end. Our team celebrated its success.
2. Confident means sure of yourself and your skills. She walked into the exam calm and confident.

How do I take good care of my books?
What does "back on track" mean?

1. Wash your hands before you read and use a bookmark, not a folded page. Keep the books on a shelf away from water.
2. It means going well again after a problem. After the holiday, we got back on track with our lessons.
What does "worth its weight in gold" mean? Also, how do I water a plant properly?

1. It means very valuable and useful. A good friend is worth their weight in gold.
2. Check that the soil is dry on top, then pour water slowly near the roots. Stop when water drips from the bottom of the pot.
What does "worry" mean? And one more: What does "slow and steady wins the race" mean?

1. To worry means to keep thinking about problems that may happen. Do not worry, the bus will come soon.
2. It means that going carefully and not stopping is better than rushing. Study a little each day, since slow and steady wins the race.

My cousin asked me two things and I am not sure.
What does "two heads are better than one" mean?
How do I make a pencil stand from a tin can?

1. It means that two people can solve a problem better than one. Let us work together, since two heads are better than one.
2. Wash the can well and cover it with coloured paper. Paste the paper on and let it dry, then put your pencils in.

What does "thrilled" mean?
Also, is it "excited" or "exited" when I am happy about something?

1. Thrilled means very excited and happy. She was thrilled to win the prize.
2. It is "excited", with an "x" and a "c". "Exited" means went out.
is it "peace" or "piece" in "a ___ of cake"? One more thing. What does "unite" mean?

1. Use "piece", which means a part of something. "Peace" means calm and quiet.
2. To unite means to come together as one. The villagers united to clean the pond.
Two small things I wondered about today. What's the meaning of "glance"? What does "don't put all your eggs in one basket" mean?

1. To glance means to look quickly for a moment. She glanced at the clock.
2. It means do not risk everything on one choice. Apply to more than one school, since you should not put all your eggs in one basket.

What does "hit the sack" mean?
And how do I clean a window?

1. It means to go to bed. I am tired, so I will hit the sack.
2. Wipe it with a damp cloth and a little soap, then dry it with a clean cloth. Wipe in straight strokes from top to bottom.
What does "stubborn" mean? what does "head in the clouds" mean?

1. Stubborn means not willing to change your mind. The stubborn donkey would not move.
2. It means daydreaming and not paying attention to real things. He has his head in the clouds in class.

What does "like two peas in a pod" mean?
What does "platform" mean at a railway station?

1. It means very alike or always together. The twins are like two peas in a pod.
2. A platform is the raised area beside the tracks where you wait to get on a train. Our train left from platform two.
What is the meaning of "polite"? Also, is it "occurred" or "occured"?

1. Polite means showing good manners to others. A polite child says please and thank you.
2. It is "occurred", with two "r"s. The "r" is doubled when you add -ed.

Need help with two things.
What does it mean to "steal the show"?
What does "squeeze" mean?

1. It means to get all the attention. The little boy stole the show at the school function.
2. To squeeze means to press something tightly. Squeeze a lemon into the water.

Please answer these two.
What is a simple way to make a banana smoothie?
Can I say "I look forward to meet you"?

1. Peel a ripe banana and blend it with cold milk and a teaspoon of sugar. Pour it into a glass and drink it fresh.
2. Say "I look forward to meeting you". After "look forward to" you use the -ing form.

Please explain "get cold feet".
Also, what does "reply" mean?

1. It means to feel nervous and change your mind before doing something. She got cold feet before the speech.
2. To reply means to answer. Please reply to my message by evening.
How do I make a paper hat? One more thing. What is the difference between "rob" and "steal"?

1. Fold a large sheet in half, then fold the top corners down to meet in the middle. Turn up the bottom edges on both sides to make the brim.
2. You rob a person or a place, and you steal a thing. A thief robbed the shop and stole the money.
Hey, got a minute for two questions? Which is right: it's or its, in "The dog wagged ___ tail"? How do I clean a blackboard?

1. Use "its" with no apostrophe, because it shows ownership. The dog wagged its tail.
2. Wipe it with a clean damp cloth from top to bottom. Let it dry before you write on it again.

What does "famous" mean?
And what does "the whole nine yards" mean?

1. Famous means known by very many people. Our town is famous for its sweets.
2. It means everything possible, all of it. They decorated the hall with lights, flowers and balloons, the whole nine yards.
What is the right spelling, "calender" or "calendar"? What does "bargain" mean?

1. It is "calendar", ending in "-ar". The calendar hangs near the fridge.
2. A bargain is something bought at a good low price. The cotton bag was a real bargain.

How do I tie a scarf?
What does "the apple of my eye" mean?

1. Fold it in half and put it around your neck so the ends hang down. Pull the loose ends through the loop and tighten it gently.
2. It means a person you love and treasure very much. My little niece is the apple of my eye.
What is the difference between "late" and "lately"? Also, what does "improve" mean?

1. "Late" means after the right time, and "lately" means recently. I was late today, and I have been tired lately.
2. To improve means to become better or make something better. Reading daily will improve your English.
What does "rumour" mean? And one more: What does "the cherry on top" mean?

1. A rumour is a story people pass on that may not be true. Do not believe every rumour.
2. It means a small extra thing that makes something good even better. The free ticket was the cherry on top.

Can you clear up two things for me?
what is the meaning of "pull yourself together"?
What does "grateful" mean?

1. It means to calm down and control your feelings. Pull yourself together, and then tell us what happened.
2. Grateful means thankful for something someone did for you. She felt grateful for her friend's help.

What does "chilly" mean?
Also, is "recieve" spelt right?

1. Chilly means rather cold. It is a chilly morning, so wear a sweater.
2. No, it is "receive". The rule is "i before e, except after c".
is it "truly" or "truely"? One more thing. What does "distant" mean?

1. It is "truly", with no "e". The "e" of "true" drops when you add -ly.
2. Distant means far away. We could see the distant hills.
Got two words to check. What does "arrange" mean? What does "hit the nail on the head" mean?

1. To arrange means to put things in order or make a plan. Let us arrange the chairs in a circle.
2. It means to say exactly the right thing. You hit the nail on the head about the problem.

I am stuck on two things.
What does "hit the road" mean?
How do I count slowly to calm down?

1. It means to start a journey. We hit the road at dawn.
2. Breathe in while you count to three and breathe out while you count to three again. Do this a few times until you feel steady.

Quick help before school, please.
How do I make my bed neatly?
What does "better late than never" mean?

1. Pull the sheet flat and tuck in the corners. Then spread the blanket and place the pillow at the top.
2. It means that doing something late is better than not doing it. You finished the project a day late, but better late than never.

What does "feel blue" mean?
How do I check whether my water bottle is clean?

1. It means to feel sad. I felt blue when my friend moved away.
2. Fill it with warm water and a drop of soap, shake it, and rinse well. Look inside and under the lid for any dirt.
Do you know what "ancient" means? Also, is it "misspell" or "mispell"?

1. Ancient means very, very old, from a time long ago. We saw ancient coins at the museum.
2. It is "misspell", with two "s"s. It is "mis-" plus "spell".
do you write "colour" or "color"? I am in India. And one more: What does "fortunate" mean?

1. "Colour" is the common spelling in India and Britain, and "color" is American. Both are correct, so use one style in the same piece of writing.
2. Fortunate means lucky. We were fortunate to find seats on the train.

Two things for you.
How do I plant a seed in a pot?
What does "off the hook" mean?

1. Fill the pot with soil, press a small hole with your finger and drop in the seed. Cover it with soil and water it gently every day.
2. It means freed from a duty or trouble. The teacher let us off the hook with no homework.

Before dinner I have to ask two things.
What does it mean to "sit on the fence"?
What is a good way to learn new words?

1. It means to refuse to choose a side. He sat on the fence in the argument.
2. Read a little every day and write down words you do not know. Use each new word in a sentence of your own.
What does "rapid" mean? One more thing. Which is correct: "I didn't see nobody" or "I didn't see anybody"?

1. Rapid means very fast. The river was rapid after the rain.
2. Say "I didn't see anybody". Do not use two negatives in one sentence.
Writing in my diary and I wonder: What does it mean to "take it with a pinch of salt"? What does "tradition" mean?

1. It means to not completely believe something. Take the rumour with a pinch of salt.
2. A tradition is a custom that families or groups follow for many years. Lighting lamps at Diwali is a tradition.

My teacher mentioned these and I forgot.
How do I make a simple puppet?
Is the spelling "neccessary" or "necessary"?

1. Draw a face on a paper bag and glue on paper hair. Put your hand inside the bag to move the mouth.
2. It is "necessary", with one "c" and two "s". Remember: one collar and two sleeves.
When do I use "already" and when "yet"? What does "dusk" mean?

1. Use "already" in a statement, and "yet" in questions and negatives. I have already eaten, and he has not come yet.
2. Dusk is the time in the evening when the light is fading. The birds flew home at dusk.

What does "patient" mean as an adjective?
Can you spell "Wednesday's" with the apostrophe? Like "Wednesday's class"

1. Patient means able to wait calmly without getting upset. Be patient while the dal cooks.
2. It is "Wednesday's class", with the apostrophe before the "s". It shows the class belongs to Wednesday.
What does "every cloud has a silver lining" mean? Also, how can I make friends in a new class?

1. It means there is something good even in a bad situation. We lost the match, but we made new friends, so every cloud has a silver lining.
2. Say hello with a smile and join in a game at break. Ask others about their favourite things.

I need your help on a couple of things.
How do I take care of a cactus?
Is it "learn" or "teach" in "She will ___ me to swim"?

1. Place it in a sunny window and water it only when the soil is completely dry. It needs very little water.
2. Use "teach", because she gives the lesson. The one who gets the lesson will learn.

Homework time and two doubts.
What does "jump the gun" mean?
What's the best way to cook plain rice?

1. It means to start before the right time. He jumped the gun and opened the gift early.
2. Wash the rice until the water runs clear, then add about twice as much water. Cook until the water is gone and the rice is soft.

What does "damp" mean?
Also, what does "tongue-tied" mean?

1. Damp means slightly wet. The towel is still damp.
2. It means so nervous that you cannot speak. He was tongue-tied on the stage.
Should I write affect or effect in "The rain will ___ our picnic"? One more thing. How do I tie a knot in a rope?

1. Use "affect", because it is a verb here. The rain will affect our picnic.
2. Make a loop in the rope and pass the end through it. Pull both ends to tighten it.
A friend and I are arguing about two things. What does "wander" mean? What is the difference between "journey" and "journal"?

1. To wander means to walk around with no fixed place to go. We wandered through the village fair.
2. A journey is a trip from one place to another, and a journal is a book where you write about your days. I kept a journal during our journey to Shimla.

Is it "cloth" or "clothe" in "She wiped the table with a ___"?
And what does "fragile" mean

1. Use "cloth", which is the material or rag. "Clothe" is a verb meaning to dress someone.
2. Fragile means easy to break or damage. Handle the glass bowl gently, because it is fragile.
What does "delicious" mean? difference between "home" and "house"

1. Delicious means tasting very good. The hot jalebis were delicious.
2. A house is the building, and a home is the place where you live and feel you belong. Their house is new, but it already feels like a home.

Is it "weather" or "whether" in "I don't know ___ it will rain"?
what does "eager" mean?

1. Use "whether", which means if. "Weather" is about rain, sun and wind.
2. Eager means keen and excited to do something. She was eager to open the gift.
what does "tidy" mean? Also, what does "lend a hand" mean?

1. Tidy means neat and in good order. Keep your desk tidy.
2. It means to help. Can you lend a hand with these bags?
Which is correct, "a lot" or "alot"? And one more: How can I be kind to a new neighbour?

1. Write "a lot" as two words. I have a lot of homework.
2. Say hello with a smile and offer to help. A small treat from home can also make them feel welcome.

Just curious about two things.
What does "nervous" mean?
What does "zip your lip" mean?

1. Nervous means a little afraid or worried. He felt nervous before his first day at school.
2. It means to stop talking or keep a secret. Zip your lip, because the surprise is coming.

what does "on the same page" mean?
Also, what does "amazed" mean?

1. It means that people agree and understand a thing in the same way. Let us meet and make sure we are on the same page.
2. Amazed means very surprised in a good way. The kids were amazed by the magic show.
How do I set the table for lunch? One more thing. Which is right: "wierd" or "weird"?

1. Put a plate for each person, with a glass on the right and a spoon beside it. Place a jug of water in the middle.
2. It is "weird". This word breaks the "i before e" rule, so it has to be learned by heart.
Little help, please, on two things. Which one is correct, "since" or "for", in "I have lived here ___ five years"? What does "relative" mean when we talk about family?

1. Use "for", because it goes with a length of time. I have lived here for five years.
2. A relative is a member of your family, such as an aunt or a cousin. All our relatives came for the festival.

What is the best way to carry a heavy bag?
And what does "over the moon" mean?

1. Use both shoulder straps and keep the bag high on your back. Take out books you do not need that day.
2. It means very happy. She was over the moon about her result.
How do you spell "scissors"? How do I make a paper fan?

1. It is s-c-i-s-s-o-r-s. It has a silent "c" after the first "s".
2. Fold a sheet back and forth like an accordion, with narrow folds. Pinch it at one end and hold it, then open the other end.

Help me with a pair of questions, please.
How do I make lemon water?
Spelling of "Wednesday"?

1. Squeeze half a lemon into a glass of cool water. Add a little sugar and a pinch of salt, then stir.
2. It is W-e-d-n-e-s-d-a-y. Say it as "Wens-day", but write the "d" after the "e".
What does "throw in the towel" mean? Also, what does "loyal" mean?

1. It means to give up. After three tries, she threw in the towel.
2. Loyal means staying true to a friend, person or group. A loyal friend stands by you.
What does "hesitate" mean? And one more: How do you spell the word for the meal between lunch and dinner, is it "snack" or "snak"?

1. To hesitate means to pause because you are not sure. Do not hesitate to ask the teacher.
2. It is "snack", ending in "ck". I had a snack at four o'clock.

Can I ask you two things?
Do we say "in the bus" or "on the bus"?
What does "pleasant" mean?

1. Say "on the bus". We also say on a train and on a plane, but in a car.
2. Pleasant means nice and enjoyable. It was a pleasant evening for a walk.

what's the meaning of "thirsty"
Also, use "say" or "tell"? Like "She ___ me a secret"

1. Thirsty means needing to drink water. We were thirsty after the long walk.
2. Use "told", because "tell" takes a person right after it. She told me a secret.
Spelling check: "definately" or "definitely"? One more thing. What's an easy way to make a fruit salad?

1. The right spelling is "definitely". It has "finite" in the middle.
2. Wash and cut some banana, apple and papaya into bite-size pieces. Mix them in a bowl and add a spoon of honey or a squeeze of lemon.
Two questions from my notebook. How can I prepare for a speech at school? what does it mean to "pull your socks up"?

1. Write a few short points and practise them aloud in front of a mirror. Speak slowly and look at your listeners.
2. It means to try harder and do better. You must pull your socks up before the final exam.

Two quick questions.
When do I use "whose" and when "who's"?
What does "adventure" mean?

1. "Whose" asks about ownership, and "who's" means "who is". Whose bag is this, and who's coming?
2. An adventure is an exciting or unusual experience. Camping by the river was a big adventure.
What does "gentle" mean? Is it "neighbour" or "nieghbour"?

1. Gentle means soft and kind, not rough. Be gentle with the baby.
2. It is "neighbour", with "eigh" in the middle. Our neighbour is very kind.

what is "a blessing in disguise"?
How can I cut a mango easily?

1. It is something that seems bad at first but turns out good. Missing the bus was a blessing in disguise, because I met an old friend.
2. Stand the mango up and slice along both sides of the stone. Cut squares into the flesh and push it out to make cubes.
Can you explain the word "harvest"? Also, tell me the difference between "accept" and "except"

1. A harvest is the time when crops are cut and collected, or the crops themselves. The farmers sing at the rice harvest.
2. "Accept" means to take something offered, and "except" means leaving out. Everyone accepted the sweets except Raj.
What does "talk of the town" mean? And one more: What does "occasion" mean?

1. It means something everyone is talking about. Her singing became the talk of the town.
2. An occasion is a special time or event. Weddings are happy occasions.

I want to be sure about two things.
How do I fold a paper into four equal parts?
Do I use "much" or "many" with the word students?

1. Fold it in half one way, then fold it in half again in the other direction. Open it and the creases make four parts.
2. Use "many", because students can be counted. Many students came early.

what does "sleep like a log" mean?
Also, how to boil milk without it spilling?

1. It means to sleep very deeply. After the long trip, I slept like a log.
2. Use a deep pot and stay close by on a medium flame. Stir now and then, and lower the flame when it starts to rise.
How can I make a sandcastle that doesn't fall? One more thing. Is it "loose" or "lose" in "Don't ___ your keys"?

1. Use wet sand and pack it down firmly into a bucket. Turn the bucket over and lift it slowly.
2. Use "lose", which means to not be able to find something. "Loose" means not tight.
Here are my two questions for today. What does "spill the beans" mean? What does "puzzle" mean?

1. It means to tell a secret by mistake. Do not spill the beans about the surprise party.
2. A puzzle is a game or problem that you solve by thinking. We finished the jigsaw puzzle together.

Getting ready for Diwali.
How can I make a rangoli?
how do you spell choclate, I think it is wrong

1. Draw the pattern lightly with chalk or dots first. Then fill it in with coloured powder or flower petals.
2. It is "chocolate", with an "o" after the second "c" and an "a" before the "t". Say it slowly as "choc-o-late".
Is it "ensure" or "insure" when you make sure something happens? how do i keep my notebook neat?

1. Use "ensure". "Insure" is about paying to protect something against loss.
2. Write on the lines, keep a ruler for headings, and cover the notebook so it stays clean. Always close it after use.

What does "companion" mean?
What does "saving for a rainy day" mean?

1. A companion is someone who is with you, like a friend. The dog is her loyal companion.
2. It means keeping something for a time when you may need it. Put some money aside for a rainy day.
do I use "is" or "are" with "news"? Also, how do I keep birds from eating my seeds?

1. Use "is", because "news" counts as one thing. The news is good today.
2. Cover the soil with a thin net or a mesh. Remove it when the plants are tall enough.
what is a good way to start a talk with someone new at school? And one more: What's the difference between "see", "look" and "watch"?

1. Smile, say hello and tell them your name. Then ask a simple question, like which class they are in.
2. You see with your eyes without trying, you look on purpose, and you watch something that moves or changes. I looked up and saw a kite, and then I watched it fly.

Last thing before bed, two questions.
What does it mean to have "butterflies in your stomach"?
How can I make a cup of hot chocolate?

1. It means to feel nervous. I had butterflies in my stomach before the race.
2. Warm a cup of milk in a pan and stir in a spoon of cocoa and some sugar. Pour it into a mug and let it cool a little.

Tell me what "journey" means.
Also, What's the difference between "beside" and "besides"?

1. A journey is a trip from one place to another. Our journey to Jaipur took all day.
2. "Beside" means next to, and "besides" means in addition to. Sit beside me, and besides rice we have curry.
What does "the last straw" mean? One more thing. What does "invite" mean?

1. It means the final small problem that makes you lose patience. The broken pencil was the last straw.
2. To invite means to ask someone to come to an event. I invited all my friends to my birthday.
I promised my sister I would find out two things. How can I remember my homework every day? What does "under the weather" mean?

1. Write it down in a small diary as soon as the teacher says it. Check the diary again before you pack your bag.
2. It means feeling a little ill. I stayed home because I felt under the weather.

What does "keep your chin up" mean?
And how to clean my spectacles?

1. It means to stay cheerful when things are hard. Keep your chin up, the next test will go better.
2. Rinse them with a little water and soap, then wipe them with a soft cotton cloth. Do not rub them with rough paper.
What does the word "sturdy" mean? What is meant by "the ball is in your court"?

1. Sturdy means strong and not easy to break. We sat on a sturdy wooden bench.
2. It means that it is your turn to decide or act. I have given my idea, so the ball is in your court.

what does "get the ball rolling" mean?
What is the meaning of "reluctant"?

1. It means to start something. Let us get the ball rolling with the first chapter.
2. Reluctant means not wanting to do something. He was reluctant to jump into the cold river.
How can I keep my pencil box tidy? Also, how do you spell "beginning"?

1. Take out everything once a week and throw away short pencils. Put the pens, pencils and eraser in their own spots.
2. It is b-e-g-i-n-n-i-n-g, with a double "n" in the middle. Doubling the "n" keeps the vowel short.

Two for you.
what is the difference between lend and borrow
what does "swift" mean?

1. You lend something to a person, and you borrow something from a person. I lend Tara my pen, and she borrows it for the day.
2. Swift means quick and fast. A swift deer ran across the field.

Can you settle a small debate between me and my brother?
What does "sincere" mean?
What does it mean when someone says "break the ice"?

1. Sincere means honest and meaning what you say. Her apology was sincere, so I forgave her.
2. It means to start a talk with people who do not know each other well. A joke helped break the ice at the party.

What does "call it a day" mean?
Also, what does "spacious" mean?

1. It means to stop working for now. We were tired, so we called it a day.
2. Spacious means with plenty of room. Our new classroom is spacious.
What does "weary" mean? One more thing. Is it "between" or "among" for three friends sharing a mango?

1. Weary means very tired. The weary travellers rested under a tree.
2. Use "among", because there are more than two. Share the mango among the three friends.
Study break! Two questions. What does "in a nutshell" mean? How do I make rose milk at home?

1. It means in a few short words. In a nutshell, we are leaving at six.
2. Mix a spoon of rose syrup into a glass of cold milk. Stir well and add ice if you like.

What does "shelter" mean?
And is it "hear" or "here" in "Come ___ and sit"?

1. A shelter is a place that keeps you safe from rain, sun or danger. We stood in a bus shelter until the rain stopped.
2. Use "here", which means this place. "Hear" is what you do with your ears.
What does "pull someone's leg" mean? What is a simple way to make a sandwich?

1. It means to joke with someone by saying something untrue. I was only pulling your leg, there is no test.
2. Spread butter on two slices of bread and add sliced cucumber and tomato. Press the slices together and cut them in half.

What does "disappointed" mean?
What does "read between the lines" mean?

1. Disappointed means sad because something was not as good as you hoped. He was disappointed when the match was cancelled.
2. It means to understand what is meant but not said. If you read between the lines, she is unhappy.
What does "the ins and outs" mean? Also, what does "crowded" mean?

1. It means all the small details of something. Ask Dad, because he knows the ins and outs of the bus routes.
2. Crowded means full of too many people. The market is crowded on Sundays.
What does "cheat" mean? And one more: What does "a green thumb" mean?

1. To cheat means to break rules or trick others to win. It is wrong to cheat in a game.
2. It means a talent for growing plants. My grandmother has a green thumb, and her tulsi is huge.

My notes are unclear on two points.
what is the meaning of "a storm in a teacup"?
How can I stay cool on a hot day?

1. It means a big fuss about a small matter. Their quarrel was a storm in a teacup.
2. Wear light cotton clothes and drink plenty of water. Stay in the shade in the afternoon.
